paper_metadata.title: Solving General QUBOs with Warm-Start QAOA via a Reduction to Max-Cut

summary: The paper studies warm‑start strategies for QAOA on 16‑variable QUBO problems (mapped to 17‑qubit Max‑Cut instances) and evaluates depths p=0–5 on simulated circuits. Across 1000 synthetic instances per problem type, the Goemans‑Williamson 2‑D warm‑start (GW2) generally achieved the best approximation ratios and sampling probabilities compared with BM2/BM3 and QUBO‑relaxed warm‑starts. Experiments are performed entirely in a noiseless custom simulator and do not include comparisons with classical optimization algorithms.

experiments.description: Warm-start QAOA for general QUBOs via reduction to Max-Cut, benchmarked on random QUBOs, TSP, portfolio optimization, and MIS instances using several warm-start constructions (GW2, GW3, BM2, BM3, and QUBO-relaxed) across depths p=0..5.

algorithm.variant: Warm-start QAOA with custom mixers / warm-start initial states; QUBO-to-Max-Cut reduction for GW/BM warm-starts
algorithm.ansatz: QAOA with custom separable mixer Hamiltonian
algorithm.convergence_criteria: fixed-depth evaluation for p=0..5; for each circuit, QAOA optimization loop run 10 times and best result selected
algorithm.parameter_initialization: For p=1, parameters drawn uniformly; for p>1, 9 of 10 initializations drawn uniformly and 1 initialized from best parameters at depth p-1

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Binary variables encoded directly into QAOA cost Hamiltonian; for GW/BM warm-starts, QUBO is reduced to a Max-Cut instance with one auxiliary variable/qubit
problem_formulation.objective_function: Maximize x^T Q x for QUBO; equivalent Max-Cut/Ising formulation used for GW/BM warm-starts
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Penalty terms for TSP and MIS; portfolio optimization uses budget penalty; QUBO-relaxed warm-start uses continuous relaxation over [0,1]^n
problem_formulation.problem_hamiltonian: H_Q^Q = sum_{i,j} Q_ij ((1-Z_i)/2)((1-Z_i)/2); H_A^M = -(1/4) sum_{i,j} A_ij Z_i Z_j

problem_instance.description: Benchmark suite of 16-variable QUBOs: random continuous and discrete QUBOs, 5-city TSP, 16-asset portfolio optimization, MIS on Erdős–Rényi and Newman–Watts–Strogatz graphs
problem_instance.dataset_name: Synthetic random QUBOs; synthetic TSP; synthetic portfolio optimization; synthetic MIS graphs

dataset_specification.description: Random QUBOs sampled from uniform [-1,1] or {−1,1}; TSP on 5 random points in [-1,1]^2; portfolio prices from geometric Brownian motion with n=16 assets and N=250 time steps; MIS on GNP (n=16,p=0.25) and NWS (n=16,k=3,p=0.5) graphs

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: TSP uses rotational symmetry breaking by fixing x_0=1; portfolio uses covariance and mean returns from simulated prices; MIS uses penalty c=1.1; TSP penalty lambda=1.1 max(A_ij); portfolio lambda=sum(|Sigma|)+sum(|mu|)
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: 1000 instances generated per problem type; 10 selected for depth p=1..5; metrics averaged with shaded regions of ±0.25 standard deviations; QAOA optimization repeated 10 times per circuit and best cost selected

implementation_details.classical_solver: L-BFGS-B for QUBO-relaxed warm-start; COBYLA for QAOA parameter optimization
implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: QUBO-to-Max-Cut reduction; SDP/BM relaxations; random basis sampling for GWk; local optimization for QUBO-relaxed warm-start
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Map Max-Cut solution back to QUBO variables; compute approximation ratio and optimal sampling probability

speedup_claims.caveats: The paper reports empirical comparisons between warm-start strategies for QAOA only; it does not claim or demonstrate a classical speedup over a specific classical optimization baseline.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: Not characterized asymptotically; QAOA depth p considered
complexity_analysis.classical_complexity: Not characterized asymptotically; QUBO-relaxed can be NP-hard for arbitrary Q, convex in special cases

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: Not analyzed; experiments run only on simulated circuits with 16–17 qubits and depth p≤5.
limiting_factors: Problem size limited to 16 binary variables
No comparison against state‑of‑the‑art classical optimization algorithms

Performance differences measured only between warm‑start heuristics within QAOA

notes: num_qubits inferred as 17 because the paper states each 16-variable QUBO maps to a 17-vertex corresponding graph via one auxiliary qubit.
